items.description: Implement the full I2P cryptographic foundation and binary serialization in pure Swift with CryptoKit: X25519 key agreement (EncType 4/5), Ed25519 signing (SigType 7) with Ed25519ph (SigType 11), ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD, HKDF-SHA256 key derivation, and SHA-256/BLAKE2b hashing. Build the I2P big-endian binary encoder/decoder for all primitive types (byte, short, integer, long, hash, string, mapping, signature, public/private keys, certificates) and the core structures: Destination, RouterInfo (identity, publication date, NTCP2/SSU2 addresses, options, signature with verification), and LeaseSet (destination, published date, leases, signature). Include round-trip serialization tests and RouterInfo signature verification.

items.title: Build the crypto and serialization core

items.description: Implement the I2P Network Database: the Kademlia-style floodfill model with XOR distance metric, DatabaseLookup and DatabaseStore message handling (query key, from hash, reply tunnels, flags, reply tokens), floodfill selection and querying of 3-5 floodfill routers, store/lookup/refresh operations, replication handling, expiration (RouterInfo ~1h, LeaseSet ~1h with 10-15 min leases), persistent on-disk storage plus in-memory cache, and startup bootstrapping that iteratively discovers peers via DatabaseLookup. Entries are only accepted after signature verification.
items.title: Implement the Network Database and floodfill DHT

items.description: Implement the NTCP2 transport per I2P spec: the Noise_XK_25519_ChaChaPoly_SHA256 handshake with SessionRequest, SessionCreated and SessionConfirm phases over TCP using the Network framework, ephemeral/static X25519 keys, padding, and key derivation into two independent ChaCha20-Poly1305 direction streams. Implement message framing (2-byte big-endian length, encrypted payload, 16-byte MAC) and the payload block types: data, time, options, padding. Support graceful session termination, connection management, and multiple concurrent peer sessions.
items.title: Implement the NTCP2 transport

items.description: Implement tunnel establishment: outbound and inbound unidirectional tunnels through multiple hops, VariableTunnelBuild messages with 528-byte encrypted request records (receive tunnel ID, next hop identity and port, layer key, IV key, reply key, reply IV, flags, padding) layered so only each hop can decrypt its record, and BuildReply handling with per-hop accept/reject codes. Build the tunnel pool per destination: 3-5 outbound and 3-5 inbound tunnels, staggered creation, expiration after 10-30 minutes, pre-building replacements, latency monitoring and tunnel selection.
items.title: Build tunnels and the tunnel pool

items.description: Implement the complete I2NP message layer: serialization and parsing of all standard message types including DatabaseStore (67), DatabaseLookup (98), TunnelBuild/BuildReply, TunnelData (18), GarlicMessage (94), TunnelGateway (15) and status/options messages, with the type byte, big-endian length, payload and expiry header format. Implement delivery instructions for local, tunnel and router delivery, plus the tunnel message processing pipeline that hops use to decrypt one layer and forward.
items.title: Implement the I2NP message layer

items.description: Implement garlic routing and end-to-end encryption: ECIES-X25519 garlic clove sets with ChaCha20-Poly1305, clove structure (encapsulated I2NP message, delivery instructions for local/tunnel/router delivery with optional delay, certificates), clove set framing with message ID and expiration, session tag management for tag-based encryption, and the wrapping/unwrapping pipeline so a destination can send garlic messages through its outbound tunnel pool to a LeaseSet's inbound tunnels.
items.title: Implement garlic routing and end-to-end encryption

Data comes from the running router's event stream.

items.description:
**Spec Compliance & Network Interoperability Review: Pure Swift I2P Router**

**Objective**
Evaluate a pure Swift I2P router implementation against current I2P specifications to verify modern cryptographic compliance, exclusion of legacy systems, and functional interoperability with the live I2P network.

**Scope: Modern Crypto Only**
- Encryption: ECIES (X25519 + ChaCha20-Poly1305)
- Transport: NTCP2 with Noise_XK_25519_ChaChaPoly_SHA256
- Signatures: Ed25519 (SigType 7) and Ed25519ph (SigType 11)
- Hashing: SHA-256 and BLAKE2b
- Key Derivation: HKDF-SHA256
- Exclude: ElGamal, DSA, 3DES, legacy signature types

**Core Compliance Areas**

1. **Data Structures & Binary Format**
   - RouterInfo serialization and certificate validation
   - LeaseSet structure and expiration handling
   - Big-endian encoding for all primitives
   - Certificate chain verification

2. **Network Database (NetDB) & Peer Discovery**
   - Kademlia DHT implementation and bucket management
   - Floodfill router identification and fallback handling
   - DatabaseLookup and DatabaseStore request/response cycles
   - Peer distribution consistency with mainnet topology

3. **Transport Protocol (NTCP2)**
   - Noise handshake phases (SessionRequest → SessionCreated → SessionConfirm)
   - Frame encryption and MAC validation
   - Session establishment and reuse
   - Interoperability with existing NTCP2 peers

4. **Tunnel Architecture**
   - Tunnel Build Message construction with encrypted TunnelBuildRecords
   - Tunnel ID assignment and management
   - Inbound and outbound tunnel pool orchestration
   - Build reply handling and failure recovery

5. **I2NP Message Protocol**
   - Correct message type encoding and routing
   - DatabaseStore, DatabaseLookup, BuildRequest, TunnelData, GarlicMessage handling
   - Message serialization and deserialization
   - Protocol version compatibility

6. **Garlic Routing & End-to-End Encryption**
   - Clove structure and nested encryption layers
   - Delivery instruction types (local, tunnel, router)
   - Expiration timestamp enforcement
   - Reply token and hop count management

7. **Router Behavior & Network Participation**
   - Proper peer selection and connection pooling
   - Lease publication and renewal cycles
   - Graceful handling of timeouts and peer failures
   - Bandwidth limiting and congestion awareness

**Validation Criteria**
- All modern crypto primitives correctly implemented via Apple CryptoKit
- Zero use of deprecated algorithms
- Successful peer handshakes with mainnet routers
- Correct DHT operations (lookup, store, peer exchange)
- Tunnel creation and data routing across real network paths
- Garlic message encryption and delivery confirmation
- Proper handling of edge cases (timeout, replay, invalid signatures)

**Testing & Verification**
- Protocol conformance against I2P specification documents
- Network connectivity tests with live floodfill routers
- Tunnel creation and data throughput validation
- Message serialization round-trip verification
- Peer reputation and bandwidth tracking accuracy
items.title: Code Review

items.description:
**Roadmap: Pure Swift I2P Router → SAMv3.3 API Socket**

**Phase 1: Complete Core Router Foundation**
Ensure all existing components are fully functional and spec-compliant before exposing them via API.
- Verify NTCP2 handshake and session establishment with mainnet peers
- Validate Kademlia DHT peer lookup and storage operations
- Confirm tunnel build and teardown cycles work end-to-end
- Test RouterInfo and LeaseSet serialization/deserialization
- Establish baseline network connectivity (3–5 floodfill connections)

**Phase 2: Implement SAMv3.3 Protocol Foundation**
Build the socket-level protocol handler independent of router logic.
- SAMv3.3 message grammar parser (Hello, SessionCreate, StreamConnect, etc.)
- Line-based protocol reader/writer with proper encoding
- Session state machine (HELLO → SESSIONCREATE → operational states)
- Error handling and RESULT message generation
- Connection lifecycle management (accept, reject, close)

**Phase 3: Session Management Layer**
Connect SAMv3.3 protocol to router destinations and tunnel pools.
- Destination creation from session parameters (private key, signature type, encryption type)
- Per-session tunnel pool initialization (inbound and outbound)
- Session-to-destination mapping and isolation
- Lease publication under session identity
- Session persistence (optional: save/restore private keys)

**Phase 4: Stream Operations (STREAM Command)**
Implement the stream build and data flow model.
- StreamConnect command parsing and destination resolution
- Outbound stream creation via tunnel chains to target destination
- StreamAccept listener registration for inbound connections
- Garlic message wrapping for stream initiation and data
- Stream ID assignment and per-stream state tracking

**Phase 5: Datagram Operations (DATAGRAM Command)**
Enable connectionless messaging via raw I2NP delivery.
- Raw datagram send via tunnel gateway
- Datagram receive buffer and delivery to client
- Datagram size limits and fragmentation handling
- Anonymous datagram support (no return address required)

**Phase 6: Naming and Destination Utilities**
Expose router name lookup and destination import/export.
- SAMv3.3 NAMING.LOOKUP for .i2p domain resolution via DHT
- Destination import (base64 public key material)
- Destination export in SAMv3.3 format
- Key format conversions (private key encoding/decoding)

**Phase 7: Socket Binding & Network Interface**
Expose the SAMv3.3 handler as a listening socket.
- TCP socket listener on localhost (default port 7656)
- Per-connection protocol handler spawning
- Concurrent session multiplexing
- Graceful shutdown and resource cleanup

**Phase 8: Testing & Interoperability**
Validate against standard SAMv3.3 clients and real network usage.
- Test with reference SAMv3.3 clients (i2p-zero, i2pd, etc.)
- Verify stream establishment to public I2P services (eepsite, IRC relays)
- Validate datagram delivery to known responders
- Load test with multiple concurrent sessions and streams
- Measure latency and throughput vs. baseline

**Phase 9: Documentation & Integration**
Prepare for production deployment in Milq iOS app.
- API documentation for SAMv3.3 command set and response formats
- Sample code for common operations (stream open, datagram send)
- Configuration guide (port, session limits, tunnel parameters)
- Error handling guide and troubleshooting reference
- Integration guide for Milq app layer

**Dependency Graph**
Phase 1 → Phases 2–3 (parallel) → Phases 4–5 (parallel) → Phase 6 → Phase 7 → Phase 8 → Phase 9

**Entry Point for SAM Integration**
Once Phase 1 is verified, Phase 2 can begin immediately as a standalone protocol handler, with incremental connection to router components through Phase 7. Phase 8 validates the complete stack against real-world usage before Phase 9 shipping.

items.description: Stage 1-3 of the alignment program as an in-app data model: a specification truth table covering every implemented structure and protocol (Destination, RouterInfo, LeaseSet, I2NP header and message bodies, NTCP2 handshake phases and frames, tunnel build records, garlic clove sets) with field-by-field wire layout, encoding rules, cryptographic parameters (EncType 4/5, SigType 7/11, HKDF labels) and edge-case rules (expiry, replay, signature rejection). Each Swift component is linked to its spec section and its Java I2P reference class (RouterInfo.java, LeaseSet.java, NTCP2Connection.java, TunnelPool.java, GarlicMessageBuilder.java, InNetMessageJob.java), with every known deviation from the compliance review classified as intentional (with rationale) or defect. Delivered as structured data (not prose only) so the alignment report can render coverage and statuses directly from it.
items.title: Build the spec truth table with component traceability

items.description: Stage 4 unit-level compliance tests runnable in the app: byte-for-byte round-trip fidelity for RouterInfo, LeaseSet, Destination, I2NP headers and each message body, tunnel build records and NTCP2 payload blocks (serialize, parse, reserialize must produce identical bytes); cryptographic cross-checks (pure Ed25519 vs CryptoKit, Ed25519ph dom2 behavior, BLAKE2b known-answer vector, ChaChaPoly/HKDF determinism, nonce96 layout); edge cases (expired RouterInfo and LeaseSet rejection, unsigned entry rejection, replayed session tags, short and oversized payloads, tampered frame MACs). Each test is tagged with a truth-table row ID from the baseline so a failure pinpoints the violated requirement. Results surface in the self-test card and feed the alignment report.
items.title: Run cross-validation compliance suite

items.description: New Alignment tab rendering the truth table live: per-component sections (Crypto, Structures, NetDB, NTCP2, Tunnels, Garlic, I2NP), each row showing its spec section, Java reference class, status (aligned / deviation documented / pending wire verification) and passing test count from the cross-validation suite; a header summary card with overall alignment coverage and last-run timestamp; a Run alignment suite button refreshing everything; tapping a deviation expands its documented rationale. Dark theme, violet accent, consistent with the I2P Core and Router tabs.

mockups.brief: Alignment report screen for the I2P router app, a new third tab beside the existing dark 'I2P Core' and 'Router' tabs. Purpose: show how closely the Swift router matches the I2P specification and the Java reference implementation, and let the user run the alignment test suite. Top to bottom: large navigation title 'Alignment' with a subtitle line 'spec truth table · Java I2P reference · Swift router'; a summary card with a big monospaced percentage (e.g. '86% aligned'), a thin progress bar in violet, and the caption 'last run 14:32 · 61 of 71 requirements verified' plus a filled rounded 'Run alignment suite' button; then per-component sections as stacked cards titled CRYPTO, STRUCTURES, NETDB, NTCP2, TUNNELS, GARLIC, I2NP — each card lists rows like 'RouterInfo serialization — spec: common/routerinfo · Java: RouterInfo.java · 6/6 tests · aligned' or 'Garlic envelope framing — ECIES-X25519 blocks · deviation documented', each row prefixed with a green checkmark circle, an orange flag circle for documented deviations, or a gray dashed circle for pending wire verification; tapping an orange row reveals an indented rationale paragraph. Palette: near-black blue background, white primary text, violet accent, green/orange status colors, monospaced numerals for counts and percentages, card corners like the existing tabs. Mood: technical, precise, calm.

items.description: Close the NTCP2 divergences from the compliance review so handshakes match real routers: derive the ephemeral-key obfuscation key and IV per the NTCP2 spec (AES-256-CBC keystream with the spec KDF, replacing the ChaCha20-Poly1305 substitution), add the message-1 options length prefix, and implement the spec's data-phase KDF for the SipHash length-obfuscation keys. All handshake, frame and negotiation tests must round-trip through the new implementation, and the NTCP2 alignment rows flip from deviation documented to aligned.
items.title: Align NTCP2 obfuscation and framing with the spec

items.description: Align tunnel data layering with the tunnel specification: AES-256-CBC layer encryption with 16-byte tunnel IVs and the full TunnelData payload layout (4-byte tunnel ID, 16-byte IV, 1008-byte body), using the per-hop layer and IV keys the pool already manages. Update the data processor, hop processing and all tunnel tests so tunnel payloads serialize byte-for-byte like real hops; the tunnels alignment rows flip to aligned.
items.title: Align tunnel layer crypto with the tunnel spec

items.description: Align the garlic envelope with the ECIES-X25519 specification: three-section new-session framing (ephemeral, static, payload sections), payload blocks (DateTime, I2NP, Options, Termination, Padding), the spec HKDF info strings for session key derivation, and the tag-based continuation rules with 32-byte session tags. Update the garlic wrapping/unwrapping pipeline and its tests so clove sets serialize to the spec shape; the garlic alignment rows flip to aligned.
